name: serve
description: Serves local directories securely over local HTTP in a lightweight background process, gated at the Cloudflare edge when published. Logs HTTP access automatically to ~/.pi-certs/logs/. Run with no directory to list what's already serving and get a suggestion for finding one. Available as the /serve command inside Pi Coding Agent, or as the standalone ./serve (or bare serve, once the repo root is on $PATH) CLI script from any other shell, including Claude Code's '!' prefix.

why.scenario: You're developing a site or web app and want a live-reloading local preview of your build output.
why.result: dist/ is served on an auto-assigned local port (8080) with live reload; the clickable URL is printed in the TUI widget. Pass --as <name> to publish it as an Access-gated preview at <name>.princess-pi.dev.

why.scenario: You forget which directory to serve, or just want to see what's already running before starting more.
why.result: serve lists the servers running in this repo, then suggests an agent prompt to locate a servable dir (e.g. "find the servable build/output dir here and serve it"). Nothing is started — you name the dir explicitly.

why.scenario: You've got stale dev servers from a previous session and need to clean them all up.
why.result: Every active server across all worktrees is terminated immediately.

why.scenario: You want to check what directories are currently being served and on which ports.
why.result: All active servers in the current worktree are listed with their URLs and access log paths.

why.scenario: You suspect you left servers running in other repos and want the full box-wide picture.
why.result: Every serve/http-server process this user is running is listed, regardless of which repo it was started from — so you can spot and kill strays anywhere.

why.scenario: You want to serve only static files (no live-reload injection) — for example, testing production builds locally.
why.result: Directories are served as plain static files without code injection or file-watching overhead.

why.scenario: You want to deploy a site to production or serve traffic to the public internet.
why.result: The serve tool is a local development preview server only — not a production web server. Use Railway, Nginx, or another production deployment tool for public-facing services.

Hide the active servers list from the screen. Pi only.
